title: Four bayou myths, checked from a kayak
why: Myth vs fact for skeptical Houstonians; includes an honest current/effort fact backed by reviews.
hook_options: Four things Houston gets wrong about the bayou
Think you need experience? Think again.
The bayou myths we hear at check-in
caption: No experience? Fine. Flat means effortless? Not always: upstream is work, downstream is a ride. Nothing to see in Houston? Herons, turtles and 300,000 bats disagree. Four myths, checked from a kayak. #buffalobayou #houstonkayak #buffalobayoukayak #houston

slides.headline: Four bayou myths, checked from a kayak
slides.body: We hear these at check-in every week. Here's what the water actually says.

slides.headline: First-timers are off in minutes
slides.body: One newbie wrote they could "navigate like a pro within minutes." Quick demo, stable boats, then you go.

slides.headline: Upstream is work. Downstream is a ride.
slides.body: When the current runs, one guest called the way up "medium or intermediate" and the way back "easy." Guides adjust routes to conditions.

slides.headline: There's nothing to see in Houston
Herons, turtles, fish, and a bat colony
slides.body: Wildlife is common along the banks, and the Waugh Drive bats fly at dusk. Never guaranteed, often surprising.

slides.headline: Fall is the sweet spot
slides.body: October and November bring cooler air and softer light. The bat colony stays year-round.

slides.kicker: Save this for the next skeptic
slides.headline: Go see for yourself
slides.body: Tours and rentals from Allen's Landing. Book at buffalobayoukayak.com.
